title: an asset specifier that escapes the project root is refused before any loader runs
notes: docs/src/pages/guide/asset-imports.mdx: 'paths outside the real project root, symbolic or hard-link aliases, conflicting shapes for one asset, and code/asset identity overlap are rejected before project output is committed.' docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md (Locked): 'Loaders use compiler-tracked asset imports rather than ambient filesystem ... access', which only holds if the tracked set cannot be widened by a specifier. `counter.json` IS staged, inside the root, and the escaping specifier is still refused, so the case measures the specifier rather than a missing file. SMITHERS5209 is the single admission gate in poc/src/build/source-assets.ts and covers both 'outside the root' and 'unreadable'; the harness compares code and authored position, not message text, so the two are one row here. The 'exists but outside the root' variant cannot be staged: the Go bridge stages a case entirely in-request and its virtualFileName refuses any input path escaping the virtual project, so a file above the root would stage on one backend only. poc/src/build/source-assets.test.ts covers that variant as a unit test. RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to refuse the program as an unresolvable untrusted foreign module (observed SMITHERS1510@1:21) rather than as an escaping asset path, so it would not have caught an escaping path that did resolve. It now reports SMITHERS5209 at the specifier; measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`.
